newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guatemalan peace talks advancing - report.
newsitem.headline: Guatemalan peace talks advancing - report.

text.p: Peace talks between lefist Guatemalan guerrillas and the government, which recently seemed near to collapse, were proceeding smoothly since they restarted on Saturday, the United Nations mediator told Mexican news agency Notimex on Sunday.
"There has been a good atmosphere for continuing the peace talks at the negotiating table and there have been no problems," UN negotiator Jean Arnault told Notimex.
The agency quoted Arnault as saying "substantial advances" had been made in the talks since Saturday, but it gave no further details.

The peace talks are aimed at reaching a definitive ceasefire in Central America's last ongoing conflict -- one that has dragged on for 36 years, leaving more than 100,000 people dead and an estimated 40,000 missing.

The talks had been running for several months when they were abruptly suspended in October after rebel commander Rafael Valdizon was arrested on suspicion of kidnapping an elderly member of an influential family that owns Guatemala's only cement company.
He was later freed in return for the release of 86-year-old Olga Alvarado de Novella.
The Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) has often kidnapped people for ransom to finance its insurrection, but promised to stop the practice.
The government of President Alvaro Arzu is aiming to have a final peace agreement in place before the end of the year.
